121	       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto

137	Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
138	Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),

146	
147	Component map (region -> spartan primitive):
148	
149	- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
150	- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
151	- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
152	- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
153	- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
154	- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.
155	
156	MVVM (the house pattern, enforced):
157	
158	- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.
159	- The component lists its VM in its own `providers: [XViewModel]` (component-scoped, NOT `providedIn: 'root'`), injects it, and binds the template to `vm` signals. The component class stays thin: no business logic, no `.subscribe`, state lives in the VM.

161	- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.
162	
163	Responsive rules (the build MUST satisfy the Part 5 gate at 375 / 768 / 1280):
164	
165	- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.

167	- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
168	- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.
169	
170	Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.
171	
172	## The off-canvas gate refinement (constitution to-do)
173	
174	Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.
175	
176	## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)
177	
178	Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. - Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.

The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.

1 --- 2 name: house-style 3 description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. 4 --- 5 6 # House frontend conventions 7 8 These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. 9 10 ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet 11 12 A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 13 14 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 15 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 16 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 17 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 18 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. 20 21 Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. 22 23 ```html 24 25
